subject.title: [Feature]: Add portable Agent Bundles for export/import across OpenClaw instances

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class core-owned portable agent bundle import/export contract, or should this be folded into existing backup/migration/plugin-bundle tracks first?
rationale: The answer decides CLI namespace, protocol schema, plugin API needs, secret/runtime-artifact boundaries, destructive import behavior, and whether this issue should remain the canonical tracker or be consolidated into related backup and migration work.

options.title: Design Core Agent Bundles
options.body: Define a first-party export/import contract with dry-run, portable allowlists, manifest validation, overwrite rules, skill/env/binding checks, and explicit exclusions before implementation.

options.title: Consolidate Into Backup/Migration
options.body: Treat the remaining work as part of the open per-agent backup/restore and cross-platform migration trackers, then close or narrow this issue after those trackers adopt the non-secret bundle requirements.

options.title: Prefer Plugin API First
options.body: Keep core lean by adding only the missing generic plugin or bundle API needed for installable agent templates while leaving packaging/distribution to plugins or ClawHub.

recommendation.title: Design Core Agent Bundles
recommendation.body: Define a first-party export/import contract with dry-run, portable allowlists, manifest validation, overwrite rules, skill/env/binding checks, and explicit exclusions before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Observed history ties steipete to agent runtime, gateway protocol, plugin-bundle docs, and repo-level product/security routing around this boundary.
